In [[algebraic geometry]], given a pair (''X'', ''D'') consisting of a [[normal variety]] ''X'' and a [[divisor (algebraic geometry)#Q-divisors|<math>\mathbb{Q}</math>-divisor]] ''D'' on ''X'' (e.g., [[canonical divisor]]), the '''discrepancy''' of the pair (''X'', ''D'') measures the degree of the singularity of the pair.
